item.title: Banks, Travel and Connectivity Reshape Practical Choices
item.description: Bank pricing, transport access, travel options and connectivity changes create several concrete decisions to revisit.
item.content:encoded:
Bank pricing, transport access, travel options and connectivity changes create several concrete decisions to revisit.

  1. More banks raise floating mortgage rates after OCR hike Kiwibank lifted its variable and offset home-loan rates by 25 basis points to 6.25% and its revolving rate to 6.30%; BNZ will add 25 basis points to variable housing rates from 17 September, and ASB is adding 25 basis points to its variable home-loan rate. 3 Sep 2026. RNZ via Otago Daily Times · Follow up
  2. Methanex plans to idle New Zealand production in 2027 Methanex agreed to sell substantially all of its remaining New Zealand natural-gas contractual entitlements from the first quarter of 2027 through their expiry at the end of the decade and expects to indefinitely idle its New Zealand methanol facilities in the first quarter of 2027. 2 Sep 2026. Methanex · Reuters · Follow up
  3. Australian dollar reaches a 13-year high against kiwi The Australian dollar traded as high as NZ$1.2285 against the New Zealand dollar, its strongest level in about 13 years; market data also recorded an AUD/NZD high of 1.2287 on 2 September. 3 Sep 2026. Market report · Twelve Data · Follow up
  4. ASB removes overseas-card margin from personal credit cards From 15 September, ASB will remove its 2.10% Offshore Service Margin from all personal ASB Visa credit cards; the 2.10% margin remains on Visa debit and business cards. 3 Sep 2026. ASB · MoneyHub · Follow up
  5. Australia gives crypto firms a final licensing deadline ASIC says digital-asset businesses relying on its sector-wide no-action position have until 30 September to apply for or vary required financial-services licences; from 1 October, firms that still need authorisation and have not met the conditions risk breaching financial-services law. 3 Sep 2026. ASIC · Follow up
  6. Rocket Lab completes its 94th Electron launch An Electron launched from Mahia at 12:01am NZST on 3 September and deployed Synspective's StriX Earth-imaging satellite into a 575km low-Earth orbit; it was Rocket Lab's 15th Electron launch of 2026. 3 Sep 2026. Rocket Lab · Follow up
  7. Edith Cavell Bridge reopens after earthquake inspection Queenstown's Edith Cavell Bridge reopened after engineers inspected it following the two Milford Sound earthquakes; the bridge had been closed overnight as a precaution. 3 Sep 2026. 1News · Follow up
  8. Belmont restores most Transmission Gully park access Most areas affected by Transmission Gully restoration work in Belmont Regional Park are now open seven days a week, including two underpasses linking the Porirua and Belmont sides; only a few motorway-adjacent sections and Cannons Head access remain restricted Monday to Saturday. 3 Sep 2026. Greater Wellington · NZTA · Follow up
  9. Wairere Falls Track closes completely for major works DOC will close the Wairere Falls Track, car park and toilets from 7 September while platforms, a bridge and other infrastructure are replaced; the department is aiming to reopen the full track by the end of November. 3 Sep 2026. DOC · Follow up
  10. Polestar prices a more practical 4 SUV for NZ Polestar has priced the new 4 SUV for New Zealand at NZ$109,900 for rear-wheel drive and NZ$119,900 for dual-motor all-wheel drive; the new body adds a conventional rear window and up to 1,680 litres of luggage space. 3 Sep 2026. EVs & Beyond · Follow up
  11. Two affordable EVs earn five-star ANCAP ratings The Leapmotor B05 and Geely EX2 received five-star ANCAP ratings under the tougher 2026 Stages of Safety criteria; both models are sold in New Zealand, giving buyers fresh crash-protection and avoidance test results. 2 Sep 2026. ANCAP · CarExpert NZ · Follow up
  12. Geely adds a longer-range Starray plug-in hybrid Geely's Starray EM-i Inspire Extended Range is now in New Zealand dealerships at NZ$52,990 plus on-road costs, with a 29.8kWh battery, 136km WLTP electric range and 60kW DC charging. 3 Sep 2026. Geely NZ · CarExpert NZ · Follow up
  13. Large used-EV study shows wide battery-health variation AVILOO analysed more than 500,000 battery tests across 20 popular EV models and found most retained roughly 87% to 94% usable capacity at 150,000km, while battery health could vary materially between vehicles of the same model. 2 Sep 2026. Financial Times · Follow up
  14. Windows will enable memory integrity on more PCs Microsoft will start automatically enabling Windows 11 memory integrity on additional eligible devices through October quality updates; devices where the feature was explicitly disabled by a user or policy will remain disabled. 2 Sep 2026. The Verge · Follow up
  15. Claude Fable 5.1 cuts cache-read costs sharply Anthropic made Claude Fable 5.1 generally available across Claude, its API and major cloud platforms; cache reads fell from US$1.00 to US$0.25 per million tokens while headline input and output prices stayed unchanged. 1 Sep 2026. TechCrunch · Follow up
  16. Qantas doubles Brisbane–Palau flights for summer Qantas will operate Brisbane–Koror twice weekly from December through March, up from once weekly, and has extended the route through at least November 2027. 3 Sep 2026. Aero South Pacific · News.com.au · Follow up
  17. Air Vanuatu restores flights to Ipota Air Vanuatu will restart weekly Port Vila–Ipota flights via Tanna on 6 September using a DHC-6-300, restoring scheduled access to Ipota after the airline last served it in 2024. 3 Sep 2026. Aero South Pacific · Follow up
  18. 2degrees tests satellite calls and data on ordinary phones 2degrees opened its Marton AST SpaceMobile ground station and completed voice calls, video calls and mobile-data tests on standard smartphones; customer-trial and commercial-launch dates have not yet been set. 26 Aug 2026. 2degrees · Follow up
